hypothesis: If the record review specifically checks that the synopsis describes a situation and trigger rather than only demographic fields, then persona theater, invented names, stock photos, lifestyle fluff, gets caught before it reaches copy.

signal.check: The avatar's synopsis reads as age, gender and income with no situation or trigger described.

prerequisites: A draft avatar record
steps: Read the synopsis field on its own, without the rest of the record.
Check it describes a situation, a trigger, and the job, not only demographic facts.
If it reads as persona theater, invented names, favorite colors, stock lifestyle details, rebuild it from real quotes.
Replace fluff fields with evidence-based fields: concerns, jobs, objections, triggers.

test.method: No paid test; this is a record-quality gate checked during review.

title: Log consent status and storage location for every interview and DM quote before it enters a brief
hypothesis: If every interview or DM quote logs its consent status and storage location alongside the transcript id, then the brand can use real customer language in marketing without a consent gap surfacing later.

signal.check: An interview or DM transcript is stored with no note on whether the customer agreed to have their words quoted in marketing.

risk.note: No quote should be used in a brief until its consent status is confirmed.

prerequisites: An interview or DM consent line used during recruitment
steps: State the recording and quoting consent line at the start of every interview or DM conversation.
Log the interview id, consent status, and where the transcript is stored, in the evidence file.
Block any quote from entering a brief until its consent status is confirmed.
Review consent terms with the brand before any interview program starts.

test.method: No paid test; this is a compliance gate checked before quotes are used.
test.read_point: Before any interview quote is used in a brief.

title: Treat 1 interview as 1 data point and cluster several before changing the record
hypothesis: If the team waits for a pattern across several interviews before rewriting the avatar record, instead of rewriting it after 1 striking interview, then the record reflects a real cluster of evidence instead of one loud voice.

signal.check: A single interview is about to trigger a rewrite of the avatar record.

prerequisites: An ongoing interview program
steps: After each interview, log the findings without immediately editing the master record.
Wait until several interviews show the same theme before changing the record.
If 1 interview rewrote the record recently, revert to the prior version and cluster the evidence first.
Note in the record how many interviews support each major claim.

test.method: No paid test; track how often single-interview record changes were later reversed.

title: Discard interview answers that came from asking about features, color, or price
hypothesis: If interviewers never ask about coils, color, firmness, price, or would you buy this, and any such answers get discarded rather than used, then the interview stays focused on the timeline and struggle that actually explain behavior.

signal.check: An interview transcript contains answers to feature, color, price, or would-you-buy questions being used as evidence.

prerequisites: An interview script or transcript
steps: Read the interview transcript for any feature, color, price, or would-you-buy question.
Discard any answer that came from such a question; do not use it as evidence.
Retrain interviewers to redirect back to the timeline and struggle questions instead.
Update the interview script to explicitly list the never-ask topics.

test.method: No paid test; this is a transcript-quality check applied after each interview.

title: List every avatar candidate before deciding how many avatars the brand needs
hypothesis: If the team lists every job candidate found across all research passes before fixing a number like we need 3 personas, then the final avatar count comes from evidence instead of an arbitrary target.

signal.check: The team is planning to build a fixed number of avatars before finishing the candidate discovery passes.

prerequisites: Candidates gathered from review mining, forum mining, interviews, tickets and surveys
steps: Pull every avatar candidate found from reviews, forums, interviews, tickets and surveys into one list.
Do not start from a target number of avatars.
Let the evidence count, first-party confirmation, and competition read decide which candidates survive.
Only after the full list exists, decide how many avatars the current cycle can support.

test.method: No paid test; this is a planning step before the priority list is built.
test.read_point: Before setting the avatar count for the cycle.

title: Never merge 2 candidates with different circumstance, consequence or emotion into 1 average avatar
hypothesis: If the priority list keeps 2 candidates separate whenever they differ on circumstance, consequence or emotion, instead of averaging them into 1 broader avatar, then creative built from the list stays specific enough to work.

signal.check: 2 avatar candidates are being merged into 1 broader record during prioritization, even though their evidence differs on circumstance, consequence or emotion.

prerequisites: A candidate list with evidence tags for circumstance, consequence and emotion
steps: Before merging 2 candidates on the priority list, compare their circumstance, consequence and emotion tags.
If they differ, keep them as 2 separate entries, even if that means a longer backlog.
Only merge candidates that share job, trigger, consequence and emotion.
Document the reason for every merge or split in the priority record.

test.method: Compare conversion between creative built from 2 kept-separate avatars and a prior averaged version, if one existed.
test.read_point: After normal test spend for each.

title: Focus creative and pages on 1 primary avatar per product line for the current cycle
hypothesis: If the brand serves 1 primary avatar per product line in creative and pages at a time, testing other avatars one at a time as backlog candidates, then everything can tune to that avatar instead of staying generic across several.
does_not_apply_when: The parent market or sub-niche is too small to support a narrow avatar (see the niche size check)

signal.check: Creative and page copy are trying to speak to several avatars at once for the same product line.

risk.note: This is 1 presenter's preference, not a proven rule; bound it with the niche size check first.

prerequisites: A prioritized avatar list with 1 clear top candidate per product line
steps: Pick the top-ranked avatar for each product line for the current creative cycle.
Build creative, page proof and language around that 1 avatar only.
Move every other candidate into a backlog with its own next research step.
Test backlog avatars one at a time, not all together, in future cycles.

test.method: Compare the scale rate of creative built around 1 focused avatar against creative that tried to speak to several at once.

title: Rank avatar candidates by first-party confirmation, evidence count, competition and size
hypothesis: If candidates are ranked in a fixed column order, dominant avatar first, then first-party confirmation, evidence count, competition read, and size basis, then the priority list reflects real evidence strength instead of whichever candidate feels most exciting.

signal.check: More than 1 avatar candidate exists and there is no consistent method for ranking them.

risk.note: Nothing should be ranked on isolation or novelty alone.

prerequisites: A candidate list with evidence counts by source type
steps: For an existing brand, rank the dominant avatar first, using the unprompted self-description tally and top-customer patterns.
Rank the rest by first-party confirmation, then evidence count, then competition read from the Ad Library, then size basis.
For a new or commodity product, rank the least-served candidate that clears the 3 proof checks first.
Record the count of avatars chosen and the reason for it; there is no fixed target number.
Re-run this ranking each quarter.

test.method: No paid test; this is the method used to decide test order, checked against later creative test results.

title: Re-check the dominant avatar and the priority ranking every quarter
hypothesis: If the dominant avatar and the priority ranking are re-checked at least each quarter or after a major channel or product change, then the mix of avatars stays current instead of drifting from what the customer base actually looks like now.

signal.check: It has been more than a quarter since the dominant avatar or the priority list was last re-checked, or a major channel or product change has happened since.

risk.note: A dominant avatar in the existing base is not proof it is the largest available market; keep testing untapped candidates too.

prerequisites: An existing priority list and dominant-avatar tally
steps: Set a quarterly calendar reminder to re-check the dominant avatar.
Re-read recent calls, DMs and reviews for unprompted self-description and re-tally it.
Compare the new tally against the last ranking and update the priority list.
Also trigger this recheck after any major channel or product change, not only on the calendar date.

test.method: No paid test; track whether the ranking actually changes at each quarterly check.

title: Build a B2B ICP layer only for a wholesale, corporate gifting or B2B line, never for the consumer avatar
hypothesis: If the TAM, ICP and persona taxonomy is built only for an actual B2B, wholesale or corporate-gifting line, and a consumer brand's priority avatar stands in for its ICP, then the team avoids inventing a company-level schema for individual shoppers.

signal.check: A consumer-only brand is being asked to fill out a TAM, ICP and buying-committee persona taxonomy meant for B2B.

risk.note: Do not invent a consumer ICP schema and attribute it to a B2B source's method.

prerequisites: Clarity on whether the brand has a real B2B, wholesale or gifting line
steps: Check whether the brand has an actual B2B, wholesale, or corporate-gifting line.
If yes, build a TAM, ICP and persona layer for that line only.
If the brand is consumer-only, use its priority avatar as the ICP equivalent, with no company-level fields.
Do not build a buying-committee taxonomy for an individual consumer purchase.

test.method: No paid test; this is a scoping decision made before research time is spent.

title: Record 2 avatars, the buyer and the user, for every gift or proxy purchase
hypothesis: If a gift or proxy purchase gets 2 avatar records, the buyer and the user, with a note on which one the creative speaks to, then copy stops accidentally writing to the wrong person in the transaction.
does_not_apply_when: The buyer and the user are always the same person for this product

signal.check: Reviews or interviews show the person buying the product is not the person using it, but the avatar record treats them as one.

risk.note: No source states this as a rule directly; it is this pass's adaptation from the B2B and proxy-decision rule.

prerequisites: Evidence that the buyer and user are different people for this product
steps: Check reviews and interviews for signs the buyer is not the user, such as gift language or a parent buying for a child.
Write a separate job statement for the buyer's decision and the user's experience.
Mark clearly which avatar the creative, page and offer are speaking to for each asset.
Keep both records linked so proof and objections from one can inform the other where relevant.

test.method: Test creative aimed at the buyer's motivation against creative aimed at the user's experience, for the same product.

title: Extend the interview timeline to cover every comparison step for a considered purchase
hypothesis: If interviews for a considered-purchase or long-sales-cycle product cover every research and comparison step before the cart, not just the moment of purchase, then the record captures the real decision journey instead of only the final click.
does_not_apply_when: The product is a low-stakes or impulse purchase

signal.check: Interviews for a high-consideration product only ask about the moment of purchase, with no questions about the earlier research and comparison steps.

risk.note: No library source gives a method for this; verify the extended timeline against the brand's own sales-cycle data.

prerequisites: A product with a known longer consideration or comparison period
steps: Confirm this product involves real comparison shopping or a longer sales cycle before purchase.
Extend the interview timeline questions to cover every research and comparison step, not only the final purchase moment.
Ask what other options were compared, and why they were dropped, at each step.
Log the comparison steps as part of the storyboard, alongside the trigger and forces.

test.method: Test page or email content addressing an early comparison-stage objection against content that only addresses the final purchase moment.

title: Write copy in the buyer's own recorded phrasing instead of brainstorming new language
hypothesis: If copy reuses the buyer's own phrases from reviews, threads and calls instead of language the marketer invents, then the pre-lander, page and creative sound like something the customer would actually say.

signal.check: A line of copy has no matching quote in the evidence file behind it.

prerequisites: An angle map pairing angles with source quotes
steps: For each angle in the angle map, find its source quote from reviews, threads or calls.
Carry the exact phrase, or a close variant of it, into the pre-lander, page and creative.
Flag any line in a draft with no source quote as invented.
Replace flagged lines with a real quote or drop the line.

test.method: Test copy built from verbatim customer phrasing against copy written by brainstorming, on the same audience.

title: Keep 1 emotional register per brief, matched to the avatar's dominant emotion
hypothesis: If a whole creative brief commits to 1 emotional register, frustration or fear, matched to the avatar's dominant emotion, instead of mixing registers, then the copy reads as consistent instead of confused.

signal.check: A single creative brief mixes frustration-driven and fear-driven lines for the same avatar.

prerequisites: The avatar's dominant emotion already named in the record
steps: Check the avatar record's dominant emotion field.
Write the brief's header to state this register explicitly, with the quotes that justify it.
Review the brief for any line that pulls from a different emotional register.
Either cut the mismatched line or split it into a separate brief for a different avatar.

test.method: Test a single-register brief against a mixed-register version of the same concept.

title: Open every hook by naming the exact situation before reaching for curiosity
hypothesis: If a hook names the exact situation in the avatar's own words before adding a curiosity mechanic, then it builds understanding first, which the source's own rebuilt examples treat as necessary before curiosity can work.

signal.check: A hook idea leads with a curiosity mechanic or a clever twist with no situational call-out naming who this is for.

risk.note: Check the situation line against the sensitive-attribute rule before it ships.

prerequisites: The avatar's trigger, failed solution and dominant fear already documented
steps: Write the situational call-out first, naming the exact circumstance in the avatar's words.
Add the curiosity mechanic after the situation is clear, not before.
Name the deepest fear the situation connects to.
Add identity phrasing that signals the avatar without stating it outright.
Check the whole hook against the sensitive-attribute rule before it ships.

test.method: Test a situation-first hook against a curiosity-only hook for the same avatar and product.

title: Run a full-funnel congruence check so the ad, pre-lander and page name the same situation
hypothesis: If the ad, pre-lander and page all keep the same named condition, setting and proof for a given avatar, then the funnel avoids the conversion drop that comes from naming one condition in the ad and a different one on the page.

signal.check: A launched or drafted funnel names a different condition, setting, or proof point between the ad, the pre-lander, and the page.

expected_effect.size: unknown, source calls a mismatch a conversion killer with no measured figure

prerequisites: A drafted or launched funnel with an ad, pre-lander and page
steps: List the condition named in the ad, the pre-lander, and the page.
List the setting shown, the proof shown, and the offer framing at each step.
Flag any mismatch and send the weaker asset back for a rewrite before launch.
Run the wrong-place test: would a non-avatar viewer feel this is not for them at every step?

test.method: Compare conversion on a congruent funnel against a version with a known mismatch fixed.

title: Show each avatar only proof and reviews that belong to that avatar
hypothesis: If a page speaks to 1 avatar and shows only that avatar's reviews and results, not mixed or generic proof, then the proof feels relevant instead of generic, and conversion for that avatar improves.

signal.check: A page built for a specific avatar shows generic reviews or results that were not tagged as belonging to that avatar.

prerequisites: Reviews and results tagged by avatar
steps: Tag existing reviews and results by which avatar they best represent.
For any page built around a specific avatar, filter proof to only that avatar's tagged reviews and results.
Remove generic or mixed-avatar proof from that page.
Flag pages with no avatar-tagged proof yet as needing more review or result collection.

test.method: Test a page with avatar-matched proof against the same page with generic, untagged proof.

title: Let the creative carry the avatar and keep Meta targeting broad
hypothesis: If avatar specificity lives entirely in the creative and the copy, not in the ad-set targeting, then broad delivery has something specific to match against instead of generic creative that gives the algorithm nothing to work with.

signal.check: An ad set is being narrowly targeted to reach a specific avatar, or a generic creative is running under broad delivery with no avatar-specific setting, story or proof.

risk.note: This folder never prescribes an audience setting; targeting decisions belong to the media and deployment team, not this note.

prerequisites: An avatar-specific angle map ready to hand to the creative team
steps: Confirm the creative carries the avatar-specific setting, language and proof, not just a mention in the hook.
Note for the media team that under broad delivery, generic creative under broad targeting gives the algorithm nothing to find the right audience with.
Keep the note that narrowing should happen in messaging, not in ad-set targeting settings.
Leave the actual targeting decision to 24-DEP and 11-ADC.

test.method: Test avatar-specific creative under broad delivery against generic creative under the same broad delivery.

title: Let the avatar's why-chain and miracles list shape the offer's framing
hypothesis: If the offer's framing borrows the avatar's why-chain and miracles list, such as reframing knee pain relief as enjoying your youth and running again, then the same product can feel bespoke to this avatar without changing the product itself.

signal.check: The offer is framed generically with no connection to the avatar's own why-chain or miracles list.

risk.note: This folder supplies the input; the offer agent still owns the final promise, price and guarantee.

prerequisites: A completed why-chain and miracles list for the avatar
steps: Pull the avatar's why-chain and miracles list from the record.
Hand these to the offer agent as inputs for framing the promise.
Check the reframed offer still describes the same real product, with no invented claim.
Test the avatar-framed offer against the brand's current generic framing.

test.method: Test an offer framed around the avatar's why-chain against the current generic offer framing.

title: Audit current and AI-drafted copy against the research file and list what to fix
hypothesis: If existing and AI-written copy get checked line by line against the research evidence file, then wrong wants, wrong words, and wrong emotions get caught and turned into a concrete gap list for the next test round.

signal.check: A copy round has shipped or is about to ship with no check against the current research evidence file.

prerequisites: A research evidence file with quotes for this avatar
steps: Read the current or AI-drafted copy line by line.
For each line, check it against the evidence file for the right want, the right words, and the right emotion.
Flag lines that miss, such as my product test failed instead of I launched and got 200 dollar CPMs.
Write the gap list and hand it to the creative team for the next test round.

test.method: Track how many flagged lines from the audit get fixed and whether the fixed version tests better.

title: Treat stalled creative testing as a signal to restart avatar research, not to change ad-set settings
hypothesis: If a stretch of tests with nothing scaling is treated as a likely research gap first, restarting review, forum and call mining before more creative variants, then the team stops burning budget on new versions of a stale angle.

signal.check: Several creative test rounds in a row have failed to scale, and the response so far has only been more ad-set counts or cost-cap changes.

risk.note: Treat this as a diagnosis to raise with the media team, not a certainty; check the test log first.

prerequisites: A test log showing several recent rounds with no scaling result
steps: Check the test log for how many rounds in a row failed to scale for this avatar.
Before running more variants, restart with a review-mining, forum-mining, or call-mining pass.
Compare fresh quotes against the copy currently being tested for a mismatch in want, words, or emotion.
Only return to creative variant testing once the research gap has been addressed.

test.method: Track whether creative built after a fresh research pass scales at a higher rate than the prior stalled variants.
test.read_point: After the next test round following the research refresh.

title: Check a creator's own audience and content against the avatar before briefing them
hypothesis: If an influencer or UGC creator is checked against the avatar's job, trigger and register before a brief goes out, then the content is more likely to sound like it comes from inside the avatar's world instead of just borrowing reach.

signal.check: A creator is being booked for reach or follower count alone, with no check of whether their own audience or content matches the avatar's job and register.

prerequisites: An avatar record with job, trigger and register defined
steps: Pull the avatar's job statement, trigger and register from the record.
Review a candidate creator's recent content and audience comments for a match to that job and register.
Reject a creator who has reach but speaks in a clearly different register or to a different situation.
Brief the matched creator with the situation line and register, not just the product features.

test.method: Compare hook rate or CTR on content from a matched creator against a creator picked for reach alone.

title: Turn the avatar's named objections and failed solutions into support macros
hypothesis: If the avatar record's objections and named failed solutions get handed to support as draft macros, then support can close a real gap the research found, the way a live-chat addition fixed a subscription brand's stated cancellation reason.

signal.check: The avatar record lists objections or failed solutions with no matching support macro or script for the support team.

risk.note: Support writes and owns the final wording; this only hands over draft content.

prerequisites: An avatar record with objections and failed solutions filled in
steps: Pull the objections and named failed solutions from the avatar record.
Draft a macro or script for each, addressing the objection directly.
Hand the drafts to the support team to write and own the final wording.
Check with support after a support cycle whether the macros are actually being used.

test.method: Track CSAT or first-reply time on tickets where the new macro was used against tickets without it.

title: Run the 4-step untapped avatar pipeline for a saturated category with no real product difference
hypothesis: If a saturated category runs the full pipeline, mainstream map, long-review candidates, Reddit validation, then deep research on the top pick, then the brand finds a genuinely different avatar instead of another angle for the same crowded avatar.
does_not_apply_when: The product has a real, checked mechanism difference from competitors

signal.check: The category is saturated, the mechanism audit found no real product difference, and creative testing for the current avatar has stalled.

risk.note: A candidate that fails size or want checks goes to the backlog with the reason; do not lower the bar just because it looks isolated.

prerequisites: A completed mechanism audit finding no real product difference
steps: Map the mainstream avatar in the Ad Library and write a who-to-avoid profile.
Mine long Amazon reviews for 3 to 4 candidate profiles with a short identifier each.
For each candidate, run a Reddit size-and-pain read and log the 3 proof checks.
Run a competitive isolation check in the Ad Library for the candidate's likely angle.
Log a demand line: keyword volume, subreddit size, or a traffic read.
Rank the most isolated candidate that passes all 3 proof checks first, keeping others as a dated backlog.
Run verified deep research on the top candidate, then assemble the full record with provisional status.
Write a rework brief listing every layer to change, and confirm with real buyers once the first ones arrive.

test.method: Track whether creative built for the new untapped avatar scales where the old mainstream-avatar creative had stalled.
test.read_point: After the first test round on the new avatar.

title: Rework a proven mass-market play for 1 avatar across every layer, not just the hook
lever: proven-play rework for a new avatar
hypothesis: If a proven mass-market angle gets reworked across claim, creative concept, page structure, primary text and proof for 1 specific avatar, instead of just swapping the hook, then the rework has a real chance to work for that avatar instead of feeling bolted on.

signal.check: A competitor's angle or format is proven to work for the mass market, and the brand wants to adapt it for a narrower avatar but has only planned to change the hook.

expected_effect.size: unknown, 1 unverified self-reported anecdote cites a 5x day-one ROAS

risk.note: Study what the proven ads claim and show; never copy their text, images, products or faces.

prerequisites: A studied, working competitor ad or angle for the mass market
steps: Study the working ads' claim and creative concept without copying their text or imagery.
Rewrite the claim, creative concept, and page structure for the specific avatar.
Rewrite the primary text and, if useful, the framing or naming, for that avatar.
Show only that avatar's results and proof on the reworked page.

test.method: Test the avatar-reworked version against the original mass-market version, on the specific avatar's audience.

title: Quantify demand with keyword volume or subreddit size before spending on a new avatar
hypothesis: If a demand line, keyword volume, subreddit size, or a competitor traffic read, is logged before committing media spend to a new avatar, then the decision to test rests on more than a rough sense of a pretty decent amount of threads.

signal.check: A new avatar is about to get a test budget with only a vague sense of demand, no keyword volume, subreddit size, or traffic read logged.

prerequisites: Access to Keyword Planner or a subreddit member count
steps: Pull keyword search volume for the candidate's terms in the target country.
Note the subreddit or forum membership size for the candidate's community.
If available, pull a competitor traffic read for a comparable player.
Log the demand line in the shortlist and let the media team size the test budget from it.

test.method: No paid test; this is a sizing input used before setting a test budget.
test.read_point: Before setting the test budget for a new avatar.

title: Store one living avatar record and evidence file per brand instead of a static document
hypothesis: If each brand's avatar records, evidence file, angle map and use log live in one queryable place instead of a static slide or PDF, then briefs can ask which quotes support this line instead of everyone relying on memory.

signal.check: Avatar work lives in a one-off slide deck or PDF that nobody reopens, with no live evidence file behind it.

risk.note: Never mix 2 brands' research in the same file.

prerequisites: The record, evidence file, angle map, and use log already built for the brand
steps: Store the avatar record, evidence file, angle map, untapped shortlist, and interview script together per brand.
Add to each record the date of last first-party evidence, the next research step, and who owns the next call.
Set up 2 standard queries: which quotes support this line, and which avatar does this brief serve.
Flag any record with no new first-party evidence in a quarter as decaying.

test.method: Track the persona usage rate after moving from a static document to a living record.

title: Book a standing weekly slot for customer calls or DMs and never let research stop
hypothesis: If the team keeps a standing weekly slot for customer calls or DMs, pulling recent and lapsed buyers, then the avatar record keeps getting fresh first-party evidence instead of relying on a one-time study.

signal.check: No customer call or DM outreach has happened in the last few weeks, and the last research push was a one-time study.

prerequisites: A customer list to pull recent and lapsed buyers from
steps: Book a weekly slot on the calendar for customer outreach.
Pull 3 to 5 recent buyers and 2 to 3 lapsed buyers each week.
Ask how things are going, then probe failed solutions, surprises, and day-to-day limits.
Log recurring frustrations and phrases in the evidence file, in the same categories as reviews.
Bring in support, fulfilment, retention or email staff to join calls, not only marketing.

test.method: Track the number of new usable quotes logged per week once the standing slot is in place.

title: Use the brand's own numbers instead of a source's self-reported figures whenever they differ
hypothesis: If the brand's own data always wins over a source's self-reported number, such as which cut of customers drives most revenue, then decisions rest on this brand's reality instead of an unverified figure from someone else's business.

signal.check: A decision is using a source's stated figure, such as top 20% of customers or 95% dominant share, when the brand's own data gives a different number.

risk.note: Where the brand has no data yet, say so in the record instead of defaulting to the source figure without a flag.

prerequisites: Access to the brand's own customer or sales data
steps: Before using a source's number (a percentage, a count, a time box), check if the brand has its own data on the same question.
If the brand's data differs, use the brand's cut and note the source figure was overridden.
If the brand has no data yet, use the source figure but flag it clearly as unverified for this brand.
Update the record once the brand's own data becomes available.

test.method: No paid test; this is a data-precedence rule checked whenever a benchmark number is used.
test.read_point: Whenever a source figure is about to be used in a decision.

title: Keep 1 research file per brand and never mix public forum quotes with another brand's private data
hypothesis: If every brand gets its own research evidence file, with public forum quotes and private interview quotes clearly labeled and never mixed across brands, then no client's private customer information ends up in another client's research doc.

signal.check: Research notes for more than 1 brand are stored in the same document, or public and private sources are not labeled by type.

risk.note: Mixing brands' private data is a trust and confidentiality risk for an agency managing several clients.

prerequisites: More than 1 brand's research in progress at once
steps: Confirm each brand has its own separate research evidence file.
Label every quote by source type: own review, competitor review, forum, interview, DM, ticket, or survey.
Never copy a private interview or ticket quote from one brand into another brand's file.
Check this separation whenever a new researcher or agent starts working across more than 1 brand.

test.method: No paid test; this is a data-hygiene check done whenever research files are set up or audited.
test.read_point: When onboarding a new brand or researcher.

title: Set up the angle map and handoff plan before a research sprint ends, not after
hypothesis: If the angle map and handoff plan already exist as the destination for a research sprint before the sprint ends, then the research does not sit unused for lack of a plan to apply it to.

signal.check: A research sprint or deep pass is running with no angle map or handoff plan set up to receive its findings.

prerequisites: A scheduled research sprint or deep-research pass
steps: Before starting the sprint, open the angle map template it will feed.
Name who receives the sprint's findings and by when, such as the creative or copy team for the next test round.
Run the sprint with this destination already in view.
Close the sprint by filling the angle map, not just the evidence file.

test.method: No paid test; track whether sprints run this way produce a used angle map versus an unused evidence file.

title: Flag any use case competitors do not target while mining reviews
hypothesis: If review mining specifically flags any use case that competitors do not address, such as post-surgery recovery for a general fitness product, then those flags feed the untapped-avatar shortlist instead of getting lost in the general review notes.

signal.check: Review mining is logging complaints and praise but not specifically flagging any use case that no competitor seems to target.

prerequisites: A review-mining pass already underway
steps: While reading 1-star and long-narrative reviews, watch for a use case that seems different from what competitors advertise.
Flag it explicitly as an untargeted use case, with the quote and listing.
Carry flagged use cases into the untapped-avatar shortlist as a candidate to check.
Do not let an untargeted use case get buried inside general review notes.

test.method: No paid test; track how many untargeted use cases flagged this way later became a tested avatar.

title: Check every promise in a creative brief is provable by the brand before it ships
hypothesis: If every promise in a creative brief is checked against what the brand can actually prove before it ships, then the brand avoids an outcome claim it cannot back up, protecting trust and reducing complaint or refund risk.

signal.check: A creative brief contains a promise or outcome claim with no evidence the brand can actually prove it.

risk.note: An unprovable claim risks refunds, complaints, and platform policy issues.

prerequisites: A drafted creative brief
steps: Read every promise or outcome claim in the brief.
For each, find the evidence the brand can point to if a customer asks for proof.
Remove any claim the brand cannot prove, even if it tested well in a similar brand's ad.
Note the proof source next to each remaining claim in the brief.

test.method: No paid test; this is a compliance gate checked before every creative handoff.

title: Attach past test wins and losses for this avatar and angle before a creative handoff
hypothesis: If the angle map carries this avatar and angle's past test wins and losses at handoff, then the creative team does not retest an angle that already failed, or forgets one that already worked.

signal.check: A creative brief is being handed off with no note on whether this avatar or angle has been tested before, and with what result.

risk.note: Requires a test log to already exist; if none exists, note that clearly instead of guessing.

prerequisites: A test log of past creative results by avatar and angle
steps: Pull past test results for this avatar and angle from the test log.
Attach wins and losses to the angle map entry before handoff.
If no test log exists yet, note that plainly instead of guessing at past performance.
Update the test log after the new test runs, so the next handoff has fresh data.

test.method: No paid test; this is a handoff-quality check reviewed before each brief goes out.

title: Confirm an untapped candidate's profile is clearly different from the mainstream avatar, not a re-skin
hypothesis: If a new candidate is explicitly compared against the mapped mainstream avatar and shown to be clearly different in profile and desire, then the brand avoids spending untapped-avatar research effort on what is really the same avatar with new packaging.

signal.check: A new avatar candidate looks similar in age, desire, or USP to the already-mapped mainstream avatar, but no explicit comparison has been logged.

prerequisites: A completed mainstream avatar map and a candidate profile
steps: Lay the mainstream avatar profile and the new candidate profile side by side.
Compare age band, desires, and USPs directly.
If they overlap closely, treat this as a re-skin, not a new avatar, and go back to review mining.
Only advance a candidate whose profile and desire are clearly distinct from the mainstream avatar.

test.method: No paid test; this is a screening check run before deep research on a candidate.
test.read_point: Before running deep research on a candidate.

title: Search the Ad Library for a candidate's angle before committing, and treat little competition as a green light
hypothesis: If a quick Ad Library search for the candidate's likely angle and keywords shows little or no advertising, then the candidate is more likely to be a real gap; if another advertiser already owns it, the proof checks should be re-run before committing.

signal.check: A candidate avatar is about to get a full research or media commitment with no check of whether another advertiser already owns that angle.

risk.note: Do not assume little competition alone proves a gold mine; it can also mean the segment is too thin.

prerequisites: Meta Ad Library access, read-only
steps: Search the Ad Library for the candidate's likely angle and keywords.
If little or no advertising shows up, treat that as supporting evidence, not final proof.
If another advertiser already owns the angle clearly, re-run the 3 proof checks before committing further.
Log the isolation check result alongside the other proof checks in the shortlist.

test.method: No paid test; this is a screening step before committing research or media budget.
test.read_point: Before committing further research or test spend.

title: Keep adjacent avatar candidates found along the way as a dated backlog instead of discarding them
hypothesis: If a candidate found during untapped-avatar research but not chosen this cycle gets logged as a dated backlog entry with its reason, then that opportunity is not lost when the team is ready to test a second avatar later.

signal.check: A promising but unpicked avatar candidate from a research pass has no record anywhere and risks being forgotten.

prerequisites: A research pass that surfaced more than 1 candidate
steps: When a candidate is not chosen for the current cycle, log it in the shortlist's backlog section anyway.
Record the date found, the evidence so far, and the reason it was not chosen this cycle.
Review the backlog at the next quarterly re-check instead of only generating new candidates from scratch.
Promote a backlog candidate to active research once capacity or a channel opportunity opens up.

test.method: No paid test; track how many backlog candidates eventually get tested versus lost entirely.

title: Build a ranked creative angle map per avatar before handing off to copy or creative
hypothesis: If every avatar gets a ranked angle map, each angle tied to quotes, register, situation line, failed solution, anxiety and proof, then creative and copy teams get a ready-to-use handoff instead of a raw research file to interpret themselves.

signal.check: An avatar record exists but there is no ranked angle map handing specific, quote-backed angles to creative and copy.

risk.note: An angle with no quote is dropped, not guessed at.

prerequisites: A confirmed or provisional avatar record with miracles, miseries, and objections filled in
steps: For each miracle and misery, write 1 angle with its quote ids attached.
Rank angles by the strength of the why-chain and the number of independent quotes behind them.
State the register from the dominant emotion, and write the situation line in the avatar's words.
List the named failed solution and why it failed, and the anxiety paired with its remover.
List which reviews and results belong to this avatar as proof.
Write the not-for line and the congruence line for the funnel.
Note cohort phrasing, platform, and any past test results for this avatar and angle.

test.method: Compare editing time and test performance for briefs built from a full angle map against briefs built from a raw evidence file.

title: Assemble the 5W profile, who, what, when, where and why, as one organized layer per avatar
hypothesis: If who, what, when, where and why are pulled together into one organized 5W layer per avatar, each field sourced, then the record gives a fast, structured reference instead of scattered notes across the research file.

signal.check: The avatar record has scattered notes on demographics, wants, timing, and location, with no single organized 5W section.

prerequisites: Who, what, when, where and why fields already researched separately
steps: Who: for an existing market, the top-customer cut compared across demographics; for a new market, competitor ads and targeting.
What: the miracles list and the miseries list.
When: life events and daily schedule type.
Where: online and offline platforms, confirmed with a platform demographics check.
Why: the benefit-to-personal-motivation chain, checked against this specific offer.
Attach all 5 fields together as one section in the avatar record.

test.method: No paid test; this is an organization step checked for completeness during record review.

title: Confirm the product passes the little-hire test before crediting a new avatar with a win
hypothesis: If a strong first-sale result for a niched avatar is checked against the repeat-purchase little-hire test before it counts as a win, then the team avoids believing a superior avatar rescued a product that does not actually solve the job.

signal.check: A niched avatar test shows strong first-purchase results, and the team is ready to call it a win before checking repeat purchase or usage data.

prerequisites: Repeat purchase or usage data for the SKU tested with the new avatar
steps: Before declaring a niched avatar test a win, pull repeat purchase or usage data for that SKU and avatar.
Compare it against the store's normal repeat rate.
If repeat purchase is weak despite a strong first sale, treat this as a product problem, not an avatar problem.
Route a confirmed product problem back to product research instead of trying another avatar angle.

test.method: Track repeat purchase rate for orders from the niched-avatar test over the next purchase window.

title: Frame every interview invite and opening as exploratory, never as sales or support
hypothesis: If the invite and the call opening both state plainly that this is not a demo, a pitch, or a support call, and give the exact time it takes, then people answer more honestly instead of guarding their words or expecting a sales pitch.

signal.check: An interview invite or opening does not clearly say the call is not a sales pitch, a demo, or support, or does not state the exact time it will take.

prerequisites: A customer list to invite
steps: Write the invite to state the purpose, learning about their experience, and what it is not, no demo, no pitch, no support.
State the exact time commitment, such as 30 minutes.
Repeat the same framing out loud at the start of the call, before the first question.
If a call drifts into support or a pitch, log it but do not use its quotes as research evidence.

test.method: Compare the depth and honesty of answers from calls with this framing against past calls that opened without it.

title: Match the interview incentive to the person, never cash to a high earner
hypothesis: If interview incentives are matched to the person, product or credit for regular customers, a charitable donation in their name for busy or senior people, never cash, then booking rates hold up without turning the ask into a rate negotiation.

signal.check: The same flat incentive, or cash, is being offered to every interview candidate regardless of who they are.

prerequisites: An interview incentive budget agreed with the brand
steps: For regular customers, offer product, store credit, or early access.
For busy, senior, or high-earning people, offer a charitable donation in their name instead of cash.
Never offer cash to a high earner; it turns the ask into a rate negotiation.
Track which incentive was used for which recruit in the evidence file.

test.method: Compare booking rates across incentive types for similar recruit profiles.

title: Track the interview booking rate itself as a signal about the segment
hypothesis: If a batch of interview invites gets tracked for booking rate, and a near-zero response is treated as a signal about the segment's weak feeling toward the product rather than only a copy problem, then the team fixes the right thing instead of endlessly rewriting the invite email.

signal.check: An interview invite batch is getting almost no bookings, and the only response so far has been to rewrite the invite copy.

risk.note: Fear that interviews cause churn is, in one source's experience, almost never founded; check bookings and cancellations before assuming outreach is risky.

prerequisites: An interview invite batch already sent
steps: Track the number of bookings per invite batch.
If bookings fill quickly, love or hate, treat the segment as one with strong feeling toward the product.
If bookings are near zero, consider changing the segment or the incentive before changing only the copy.
Log cancellation rates too, to check whether fear of causing churn is actually founded for this brand.

test.method: Compare booking rate after changing the segment or incentive against the rate from the copy-only rewrite.

title: Run direct calls and DMs to buyers on the channel they actually use, asking what surprised them
hypothesis: If direct calls and DMs run on the specific channel buyers actually use, asking what surprised them, then the brand gets ongoing first-party language without waiting for a formal interview program.

signal.check: The brand has not identified which DM channel or platform its buyers actually use for direct outreach.

prerequisites: Knowledge of which DM channel and platform the brand's buyers actually use
steps: Confirm which DM channel and platform this brand's buyers actually use.
Reach out directly on that channel, asking what surprised them about the product or their situation.
Listen for unprompted self-description and tally it.
Treat DM outreach as underrated and standing, not a one-off effort.

test.method: Track the number of usable quotes gathered through DM outreach per month.

title: Run a post-purchase or verification survey after interviews, never before, to count what they found
hypothesis: If a survey is designed after interview themes are known and used only to verify and count those themes at scale, with careful wording, then it confirms real findings instead of introducing wishlist answers or biased results.

signal.check: A survey is being planned as the first or only research step for a new avatar, before any interview themes exist.

risk.note: Leading questions, positive-only phrasing, and question order can all skew results; pilot on a small group first.

prerequisites: Interview themes already identified
steps: Design survey questions from the themes interviews already found.
Fire a post-purchase survey after checkout, with an email follow-up, asking what was going on when they bought and what they tried.
Check wording for leading questions, positive-only phrasing, and question order bias.
Pilot the survey on about 5 people before sending it wide.
Aggregate results; treat a brand-new theme that only the survey shows as unconfirmed until interviews back it up.

test.method: Compare the themes the survey confirms against the original interview themes for consistency.

title: Never use a feature-request survey or a focus group to discover a new job
hypothesis: If feature-request surveys and focus groups are never used as the discovery method for a new job, since they produce wishlists instead of real jobs, then research time goes to timeline interviews and behavioral data instead.

signal.check: A PDP feature-vote widget, a reviews-page poll, or a room-based focus group is being used to decide what job a new avatar has.

risk.note: This does not ban a well-built verification survey run after interviews; it bans using either as the discovery method.

prerequisites: None
steps: Check whether a planned feature-vote widget, poll, or focus group is being used to discover a job, not just to verify one.
If it is for discovery, replace it with timeline interviews and behavioral data instead.
Keep a well-built verification survey for after interviews have already found a theme.
Note in the record that focus groups and feature surveys were avoided for discovery, and why.

test.method: No paid test; this is a method check applied before choosing a research tool.
test.read_point: Before designing a new-job discovery study.

title: Mine support tickets, call transcripts and return reasons as passive struggle data
hypothesis: If support tickets, call transcripts and return reasons get mined and tagged by theme with counts and dates, then the record gets passive evidence of struggle and unmet jobs that active sales data alone would miss.

signal.check: The brand has a helpdesk or returns log, but nobody has pulled themes from it for avatar research.

risk.note: Do counts in code, not by eye.

prerequisites: Access to support tickets, call transcripts, and return or cancellation reasons
steps: Export support tickets, sales or support call transcripts, and return and cancellation reasons for the period.
Read for recurring pains, who is asking (proxy or gift buyers), workarounds, and returns describing a wrong job.
Tag each theme with a count and dates, quoting 2 or 3 tickets per theme by ticket id.
Feed workarounds into candidate jobs, and wrong-job returns into the not-for line.

test.method: No paid test; compare avatar candidates found through ticket mining against those found through reviews alone.

title: Storyboard the customer's struggle to surface the forces and the trigger moment
hypothesis: If interview notes get turned into a simple storyboard, once upon a time, every day, one day, because of that, finally I did, then the forces and trigger moment become clear and datable instead of staying buried in loose notes.

signal.check: Interview notes exist for an avatar, but no one has organized them into a clear situation, routine, trigger, and resolution sequence.

prerequisites: Interview or research notes for the avatar
steps: Write once upon a time as the starting situation.
Write every day as the routine and its workaround.
Write one day as the dated trigger event.
Write because of that and because of this as what they tried, what was fired, and the 4 forces.
Write finally I did as the purchase and what removed the last anxiety.
Mark each moment with a quote, or note it as inferred if no quote supports it.
Hand experiential moments, such as unboxing and first use, to the post-purchase and landing page teams.

test.method: No paid test; this organizes existing evidence into the trigger and forces fields.
test.read_point: After interviews, before the record is finalized.

title: Record every trigger moment as a datable event, covering life events and daily schedule
hypothesis: If every avatar record captures its trigger as a specific, datable event rather than a vague mood, and covers both life events and daily schedule, then the timing field can inform when and where to reach this avatar, not just why.

signal.check: The avatar record's trigger field is a vague mood or general statement instead of a specific, datable event with a quote.

prerequisites: At least 1 interview or detailed quote describing a purchase trigger
steps: Search quotes for a specific, dated moment that triggered the purchase, not a general feeling.
Note life events, such as marriage, divorce, a new child, a new job, or moving, that shifted buying.
Note daily schedule type, such as 9-to-5, stay-at-home parent, or home entrepreneur, that shifts when and where they buy.
Attach at least 1 quoted trigger event to every record.

test.method: No paid test; this is a record-completeness check during review.
